subsystems.name: Imaging and sectioning
subsystems.role: capture the brain's wiring at the resolution of individual synapses, which are nanometres across.
parts: automated cutting or milling of tissue into nanometre slices

subsystems.name: Image processing
subsystems.role: turn exabytes of microscope images into a traceable wiring diagram.

subsystems.name: Connectome and cell mapping
subsystems.role: record which neuron connects to which, and what type each one is.

subsystems.name: Neuron and synapse models
subsystems.role: describe mathematically how each cell and connection behaves.

subsystems.name: Simulation platform
subsystems.role: run the model of the brain on computing hardware.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and interface
subsystems.role: give the simulated mind senses, actions and a way to communicate.

subsystems.name: Validation
subsystems.role: test whether the emulation actually reproduces the original mind's behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the brain
buildSteps.detail: Perfuse and fix the tissue so that structure survives fixation without distortion; for a living person this step, and what it means ethically, is unresolved.

buildSteps.title: Slice and image
buildSteps.detail: Cut the brain into nanometre-thin sections and image each with an electron microscope, producing many petabytes of images. Imaging one whole human brain this way is far beyond current throughput.

buildSteps.title: Segment the images
buildSteps.detail: Machine-learning models trace every neuron's branching shape and mark each synapse, then human proofreaders correct the errors.

buildSteps.title: Build the connectome
buildSteps.detail: Assemble those traces into a graph of roughly 10^14–10^15 synapses, and add molecular data on cell type and neurotransmitter.

buildSteps.title: Model the cells
buildSteps.detail: Turn each traced neuron into equations describing its membrane, channels and synapses; use functional recordings where they exist to set the parameters.

buildSteps.title: Simulate
buildSteps.detail: Connect the model neurons and step the whole network forward in time on large computing hardware. Real-time or faster operation is an enormously larger task than the wiring diagram alone.

buildSteps.title: Embody and test
buildSteps.detail: Give the running simulation senses and outputs, then compare its behaviour against recordings of the original person.

buildSteps.title: Run on durable hardware
buildSteps.detail: Once verified, the process can in principle be copied and run on whatever computing substrate is fastest and most reliable, rather than on a biological body.

prerequisites.why: electron microscopy can trace small volumes — the complete brain of a fruit fly and a cubic millimetre of mouse cortex have been mapped — but a whole human brain is millions of times larger.
human proofreading is still the bottleneck in every connectome project, and brain-scale data volumes are extreme.
simulating neurons is feasible, but simulating 86 billion detailed neurons with realistic synapses at real speed is far beyond today's largest machines.

prerequisites.tech: A theory of how memory and computation sit in the synapses
prerequisites.why: structure alone does not reveal the strength or state of each connection, which is where much of what a mind does is thought to reside.

prerequisites.tech: Ethical and legal framework for emulated minds
prerequisites.why: if an emulation is a person, questions of consent, copying and ownership arise immediately and have no settled answers.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of very small nervous systems and of a fruit fly, plus dense reconstructions of small mammalian cortex volumes
pathway.unlocks: scaling methods for sectioning, imaging and automated tracing.

pathway.milestone: a whole mouse brain connectome linked to functional recordings
pathway.unlocks: the first realistic chance to test whether structure predicts behaviour in a mammal.

pathway.milestone: emulation of small, well-understood brain circuits that reproduce measured outputs
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the modelling approach can work before attempting a whole brain.

pathway.milestone: a whole human brain scan and emulation validated against the original person
pathway.unlocks: substrate-independent minds in principle, with all the unresolved ethical questions that follow.

pathway.milestone: running minds copied onto durable, engineered hardware
pathway.unlocks: intelligence that is not tied to a finite biological lifespan or to Earth's environment — the point of the idea, and its least certain part.
